transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-08
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood CSM), Lena Ortiz (Verdance Head of ML), Marcus Ye (Verdance Platform Eng), Rita Huang (Verdance Security), Tom Calder (Verdance Procurement)

Summary (auto): Quick renewal/expansion check to move Verdance from pay-as-you-go to a 12-month committed plan with dedicated capacity and an on‑prem pilot for EU region. Action items captured. Transcription has some mis-hears.

Transcript:
00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick check-in, hopefully this is a productive 45 min. We wanted to review the capacity uplift options and align on the on‑prem pilot timeline. Lena, do you want to kick off with where you are today?
00:22 Lena (Verdance): Yeah thanks Alex. We are seeing a steady uptick, week over week. Our current hosted usage is about 4 million tokens/day and peak bursts hit roughly 120 qps for short windows. The trick is EU latency; our users in EMEA want sub‑150ms tail for short replies so we're prioritizing an EU on‑prem pilot.
00:41 Samira (Redwood SE): Got it, 4M tokens a day and 120 qps bursts. That matches what we saw in the telemetry you shared. For sub‑150ms tails we'll probably recommend a regional dedicated pool plus local KV cache. One note though — when you say on‑prem, do you mean full air‑gapped on‑prem or a VPC private deployment?
01:03 Marcus (Verdance): At first it's private VPC in our EU colo. We want to keep control of keys, integrate with our HSM, but not fully air‑gapped at pilot start. If that works we may expand to a tighter on‑prem install later.
01:19 Alex (Redwood AE): Perfectly reasonable. That maps to our Redwood Private flow — private control plane, customer-managed VPC, KMS/HSM integration. Rita, from security perspective any blockers?
01:30 Rita (Verdance Security): Overall okay but we need to validate encryption at rest + key rotation behavior with our HSM. Also we need a SOC2 report and more detail on audit logs retention per request. A quick red team/pen test schedule would be nice.
01:45 Samira (Redwood SE): We can provide SOC2 artifacts and an audit log sample. Small heads up: some of the field names in the audit log are redacted by default, and the KV cache reference may be transcribed as K V cache in older reports — sorry if that caused confusion in the docs.
02:01 Tom (Procurement): From procurement, we're evaluating a 12‑month commitment. Price sensitivity is real — if we commit to dedicated capacity we need predictable unit economics. How flexible are the tiers?
02:12 Alex (Redwood AE): We have three recommended tiers for dedicated: Small (reserved baseline + burst), Medium (higher baseline with lower per-token overage), and Large (committed baseline with priority routing). I can send a chart with the per‑token effective price at different utilization rates. We also have an option for a phased ramp with a 6‑month check point.
02:33 Lena: That phased ramp sounds good. We want the ability to scale fast if an experiment goes viral. Also curious about fallback behavior — if the dedicated pool is saturated, will we route to hosted variants?
02:44 Samira: Yes, routing policies can failover to a compatible hosted model variant. It's configurable per route so you can decide latency vs cost tradeoffs. For your EU pilot we'd likely set a strict priority to keep traffic local during SLO hours and allow fallback outside of peak windows.
03:02 Marcus: For the throughput benchmark you proposed — what's the plan? We want results that mirror our real payloads, not just synthetic prompts.
03:12 Samira: Plan is to run a 72‑hour run with two instance sizes: one matching your estimated baseline and one higher headroom instance. We'll replay a sampled trace you provide, including average seq length and top prompt families. We'll produce latency P50/P95/P99 plus token cost estimates.
03:32 Marcus: I'll export the traces after the call. Note, our distribution has a long tail — a small % of requests hit 1k tokens. Hope that won't throw the benchmark.
03:40 Samira: We'll parametrize the seq length distribution. If you can give a histogram that would help.
03:45 Rita: Security question — when we hand over traces, can we mask PII easily? We need an NDA with redactions.
03:53 Alex: Yes, we can accept redacted traces. Also we have a data handling addendum we can share. I'll attach it with the pricing doc.
04:02 Tom: On pricing — is there a cap on overage? We need predictability.
04:08 Alex: Yes, contracts can include an overage cap or accelerators. For example a +20% overage safety buffer at a blended rate, or hard cap with automatic throttling (not ideal for UX). We have options.
04:20 Jordan (CSM): Also we can enable per‑token cost dashboards for your team so you can see which routes are driving spend. That usually helps procurement feel better.
04:28 Lena: Good. Two calendar notes: we want the pilot in EU in May if possible, and we need procurement signoff by mid‑June to hit a July 1st go‑live for full commit. Is that timeline doable?
04:41 Alex: Tight but doable if benchmarks finish mid‑April and security checks move fast. We should aim to complete benchmarks by 4/15, security checklist by 4/13, and draft contract by 4/20.
04:53 Marcus: One more technical deep dive question — quantization and model variants. We're using an Llama‑style open model. Can Redwood run int8 or 4‑bit quantized variants in the dedicated pool? Does that affect latency variability?
05:07 Samira: Yes we support quantized variants. Latency depends on sequence length and kernel selection — quantization generally reduces memory pressure and can lower cost, but for short low‑seq requests you sometimes see smaller latency improvements. We'll include quantized vs fp16 tradeoffs in the benchmark report.
05:24 Rita: Also, what about auditability of model changes during the contract — if you update an internal kernel or patch, will we see versioning? We need model version pinning for compliance windows.
05:34 Samira: We support model pinning per deployment and can surface kernel/engine version in the runtime metadata. Rollouts can be canaryed and you can opt out of automatic upgrades.
05:44 Tom: Procurement question — do you offer net‑30 invoicing for committed contracts?
05:48 Alex: Yes, for enterprise commitments we support net‑30 and net‑45 depending on credit checks. I'll have finance include terms in the contract draft.
05:55 Lena: Okay next practical thing, who owns the on‑prem install — Verdance ops or Redwood infra?
06:02 Alex: For a private VPC deployment, Verdance ops will own the host infra and keys, Redwood will provide the control plane and runtime artifacts. For a fully managed on‑prem we can provide an ops bundle but it's a different pricing/engagement. Pilot is VPC, so you'll own hosts.
06:18 Marcus: Great. I'll share infra contacts after this call.
06:21 Samira: Quick note — some logs in older docs show 'K V cache' spaced out, may just be transcription artifact, not product change.
06:28 Rita: Noted.
06:30 Alex: Alright let's recap next steps: I'll send pricing + contract template by 4/12, Samira will run the 72h benchmark and post results by 4/15, Rita to send security checklist by 4/13, Marcus to share traces and infra contacts by 4/11. We tentatively schedule pilot kickoff the week of 4/20. Any other questions?
06:53 Lena: One more — do you have references for EU private pilots? Would be helpful to see a short case study.
07:00 Jordan: Yes, we'll share a redacted case study (two pager) from a recent financial customer who did a similar EU VPC pilot.
07:08 Tom: That helps procurement.
07:10 Alex: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with links and docs.
07:14 (call ends)

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis‑labels and filler words present; some proper nouns slightly off (e.g., K V cache vs KV cache).
